memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But he refused. 'With me in charge,' he told her, 'my master does not concern himself with anything in the house; everything he owns he has entrusted to my care. No one is greater in this house than I am. My master has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?'" - Gen 39:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph's answer is immediate and clear: "But he refused." No hesitation, no negotiation. And listen to his reasons. First, he thinks of his master's trust: Potiphar had entrusted everything to him, holding nothing back except his wife; to betray that trust would be a deep wrong. Joseph honoured the confidence placed in him even when no one was watching.

But his deepest reason rises above all else: "How then could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?" Joseph understood that this was not merely a private matter, not just a betrayal of Potiphar — it was, above all, a sin against God. He saw his moral choices in the light of the Lord he served.

This is the heart of true integrity. Joseph resisted not mainly because he might be caught, or because of the harm to others, but because sin is fundamentally an offense against a holy God. Centuries later, David would confess after his own sin, "Against you, you only, have I sinned" (Ps 51:4). When we see sin the way Joseph did — as an offense against the God who loves us — we find a far stronger reason to resist it.

What keeps you from sin? Fear of consequences fades, and no one may ever know. But a heart that loves God and refuses to grieve Him has an anchor that holds. Learn to ask Joseph's question: "How could I sin against God?"

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see sin primarily as an offense against God?
2. What most keeps me from sin — fear of getting caught, or love for God?
3. How would asking "How could I sin against God?" change my choices?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to see sin as You see it — an offense against You. Give me a heart that loves You too much to grieve You, so that I resist temptation for Your sake. Amen.
